name: Jay Obernolte
stance: Wants a federal AI framework with frontier-model transparency and independent verification, paired with temporary preemption of state laws regulating AI development.

statements.text: Congress must enact a single unified federal regulatory framework for AI to avoid a complex patchwork of conflicting state laws.
Introduced H.R. 3460, the AI Whistleblower Protection Act, to protect people who report potential risks in AI systems from retaliation.
Those who identify potential risks in artificial intelligence systems must be able to speak up without fear of retaliation.

I highlighted the need for Congress to do its job by putting a clear federal framework in place for AI so the United States can remain safe, competitive, support innovation, and address national security risks as this technology continues to advance.
We discussed the risks of a patchwork of state AI laws, the importance of regulatory clarity, and what U.S. companies need to grow and invest here at home.
I applaud the White House’s continued leadership in advancing a national policy framework for artificial intelligence.

Released the Great American Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026 discussion draft with Rep. Trahan: frontier developers must publish risk frameworks and retain independent verifiers, CAISI is codified, and state AI development laws are preempted for three years.

This discussion draft is an important step toward building a clear federal framework that promotes innovation, protects Americans from emerging risks, and ensures the United States continues to lead the world in AI.
Congress needs to do its job in regulating this new technology with a clear national framework that protects Americans while ensuring the United States remains the global leader in AI.

His AI Security and Innovation Act, which would establish a Center for AI Security and Innovation with federal evaluation capabilities for emerging AI risks, was advanced by the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee.
His READ AI Models Act, creating a framework for documenting AI models and their data to improve transparency and risk management, was advanced by the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee.
Said upcoming revisions to the draft could absolutely include a rewrite of how it handles state laws.

With Rep. Trahan, introduced the FRONTIER Act (H.R. 9925), a national framework of tiered model cards, risk-management frameworks, independent audits and incident reporting for the most advanced AI systems.
This legislation will protect Americans from catastrophic risk
Introduced the bipartisan FRONTIER Act with Rep. Lori Trahan, setting national rules for the largest AI developers including transparency, independent evaluations and reporting of serious incidents.
This legislation builds on our Great American AI Act framework to protect Americans from catastrophic risks and ensure the United States remains the global leader in AI.
America needs a national framework that protects innovation while establishing clear rules of the road for the most advanced AI systems.
At a Science Committee hearing, pressed OSTP Director Michael Kratsios on ensuring the Center for AI Standards and Innovation has the resources needed to evaluate advanced AI systems.
Advanced AI raises important questions about safety and accountability, but stopping American innovation is not the answer.
There are real risks associated with increasingly advanced AI systems, but we must mitigate those risks while still allowing the beneficial uses of AI to thrive.
The United States can address the real risks posed by artificial intelligence while ensuring our regulatory approach does not undermine American innovation and global leadership in AI.
As these systems grow more capable, Congress needs to understand the risks they present and ensure developers have appropriate processes to identify and address them.

The creation of the new White House task force on advanced AI is an important step toward ensuring America remains the global leader in this transformative technology while addressing the risks posed by the most advanced systems.
AI is advancing rapidly, and Congress has an important role to play in addressing the most serious risks without undermining American innovation.
